label: Current frontier
peers: Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (Sep 1), GPT-6 Astra (Sep 4), Gemini 4 Argon (GA Oct 13). Opus 5.5 is the frontier: AA #1 (58), ECI 169 tied with GPT-6 Astra
highlights: Terminal-Bench 4.0 66.4% vendor / 59.6% independent; OSWorld 2.0 81.8% partial but 48.7% strict
METR: an "incremental improvement above Fable 5.1" with limited gains in judgement or taste
definition: Share of the time professionals currently spend on a task that the best publicly available model could do at the quality of a competent professional, with no more than light review, given tools and integrations reasonably available at the time. It measures technical capability, not adoption.
method_note: Scores triangulate expert-parity rates (GDPval), reliability-adjusted time horizons (METR 80%), end-to-end automation rates (Remote Labor Index), narrow agentic benchmarks and labor-side studies. Forecasts close each task type's gap to its ceiling at the pace of the last ten months. See reports/AI saturation of white collar work.md.
caveats: Scores are calibrated judgments, not direct measurements. Sales, scheduling, compliance, bookkeeping and 2026 translation have no benchmark with published model scores.
Most 2026 benchmark figures are vendor-reported and reached through secondary sites. No independent METR time horizon exists for any model released after May 2026.
Earlier snapshots score the best publicly available model on each Opus release date, excluding gated models such as Mythos Preview.
Forecast uncertainty is about ±5 points per task type at F+1 and ±8 at F+2, wider for judgment-heavy work.

evidence.draft: Expert-graded GDPval wins-or-ties rose from 47.6% (Opus 4.1) to 80.3% (Opus 4.7) and 84.9% (GPT-5.5); Opus 5.5 now leads Elo-based GDPval-AA at 1846–1866, +138 over Opus 5. Residual misses are instruction-following and missing context.
evidence.edit: No dedicated benchmark; writing and communicating show the highest completion in Microsoft's 200k Copilot conversations, Opus 4.6 scored 76% on 1M-token MRCR retrieval, and GDPval deliverables reached ~85% expert parity by April 2026.
evidence.translate: Microsoft ranks interpreters and translators among the most AI-applicable occupations and WMT25 organizers called standard test sets too easy, but no 2026 benchmark with model scores exists, and live clinical or courtroom interpretation still needs presence.
evidence.research: BrowseComp rose from 84.0% (Opus 4.6) to 90.8% (Opus 5) and HLE-with-tools from 53.0% to 67.7% (Opus 5.5), but Harvey's BigLaw research set targets case-law problems leading models cannot solve, so citation checking persists.
evidence.analysis: Opus 4.6 scored 61.8% against human experts' 77.2% on FrontierFinance; Vals Finance Agent rose 58.8%→64.4% (Opus 4.5→4.7); real-workbook SpreadsheetBench V2 tops out near 35%; Opus 5.5 cut an internal financial-modeling task from 93 to 63 minutes.
evidence.expert: Opus 4.6 scored 90.2% on BigLaw Bench core tasks, yet APEX-Agents law Pass@1 was 29.7% in March 2026, jurisdiction-specific work degrades, and METR found Opus 5.5 showed limited gains in judgement or taste.
evidence.diagnosis: OpenAI's own HealthBench Professional scored GPT-5.4 at 59.0 versus physicians' 43.7 and Vals archived MedQA as saturated, but ESADE classes diagnosis as expert complementarity (44.2% of family-physician time) and no independent real-world validation exists.
evidence.code: SWE-bench Pro climbed 53.4% (Opus 4.6) → 64.3% → 69.2% → 79.2% (Opus 5); METR's 80% horizon rose from 19 minutes (Opus 4.1) to 70 minutes (Opus 4.6) and 3h06m (Mythos Preview); harder FrontierCode sits at 54.4%.
evidence.debug: Terminal-Bench 2.0 rose from 59.3% (Opus 4.5) to 69.4% (Opus 4.7), with GPT-5.3-Codex and GPT-5.5 at 77–83%; harder TB 4.0 went 52.3% → 66.4% from Opus 5 to 5.5 (59.6% independently measured).
evidence.design_tech: No direct benchmark. Agents now finish 680,000-line migrations in under a day, but METR saw limited judgement and taste gains in Opus 5.5, and CAIS found Fable 5's CAD and architecture deliverables unacceptable as finished work.
evidence.entry: OSWorld-Verified climbed from 66.3% (Opus 4.5) to 83.4% (Opus 4.8), past the 72.4% human baseline; SpreadsheetBench V1 is ~99% but 12–14% of tasks flip between runs, and strict OSWorld 2.0 success is only 48.7%.
evidence.docproc: No claims-processing benchmark; Vals archived MortgageTax and similar QA sets as saturated, GDPval models neared expert parity in government and retail tasks, and Office & Admin API traffic rose to 13%; exception handling keeps scores below data entry.
evidence.accounting: No public month-end-close leaderboard exists (AccountingBench publishes none); real-workbook SpreadsheetBench V2 tops out near 35% and Tax Agent Bench ranks Opus 5.5 third, so zero-error reconciliation still demands real checking.
evidence.compliance: Policy-following is strong (tau2 agents 82–99%; LegalBench led by Fable 5), but no compliance-review benchmark exists, ESADE puts 44.7% of legal time in tacit expert judgement, and attestations need a named accountable human.
evidence.scheduling: No scheduling benchmark; tau2 airline rebooking under policy reaches 82–88%, computer use passed the human OSWorld baseline in March 2026, and Cowork (January) plus Claude in Chrome (GA August) added calendar and browser access; multi-party coordination is unmeasured.)
evidence.project: Opus 5 grew a simulated vending business to $11,182 on Vending-Bench 2 but reportedly broke promises doing so; AutomationBench reached 40.0% and RLI 21.25% (Opus 5.5), while the reliable horizon of hours trails multi-week projects.
evidence.service: tau2 telecom saturated at 99.25% (Opus 4.6), with retail ~85% and airline 82–88%; Anthropic's observed-exposure study ranks customer service representatives second only to programmers, but live channels need every answer right, not 85% of them.
evidence.support: tau2 telecom, a simulated user-troubleshooting task, is saturated near 99%, and OSWorld-Verified reached 83.4% (Opus 4.8) and ~90% by October 2026, but strict OSWorld 2.0 success is 48.7% and hardware fixes stay on-site.
evidence.creative: No concept-quality benchmark; CAIS reports hours-long digital art now done in minutes and 80% of Claude marketing-content conversations are work, but METR saw limited taste gains in Opus 5.5 and ESADE's authorship factor keeps credited ideas with people.
evidence.media: Remote Labor Index rose from 2.5% (October 2025) to 21.25% (Opus 5.5), yet CAIS judged Fable 5's 2D video ads, 3D/CAD and architecture deliverables unacceptable, and Microsoft found image generation among the lowest-success Copilot activities.
evidence.grading: Vals' SAGE grading benchmark ranks Opus 4.7 first (scores unpublished), Educational Instruction rose from 9% to 15% of Claude.ai use, and rubric-style text work is near parity; teachers still own grades and sensitive feedback.
evidence.teaching: ESADE rates presence-requiring tasks 14.1% replaceable versus 70.5% for purely informational ones; AI explanation is strong in chat, but classroom instruction and behaviour management need an accountable adult in the room.
evidence.sales: No benchmark; sales-outreach automation at least doubled its share of Claude API traffic by February 2026 and Microsoft scores services sales reps 0.35 applicability, but Opus 5 reportedly broke 11 supplier promises on Vending-Bench, illustrating trust risk.
evidence.relationship: No benchmark exists; ESADE's relational-nexus bundling factor is nearly uncorrelated with exposure (correlation of at most 0.13), and Stanford finds employment flat or rising where AI complements experienced workers; AI drafts the check-in, the trust accrues to people.
evidence.meetings: Notes and summaries score under editing; live participation is the human contribution. Microsoft finds the AI's own actions centre on communicating, which supports async answers, but no benchmark measures a model standing in for a participant.
evidence.people: Management is only 3–5% of Claude.ai conversations, ESADE's organisational-responsibility factor keeps hiring and performance decisions with a person, and screening or drafting subtasks score elsewhere, leaving AI a support role.
evidence.strategy: Mercor's APEX-Agents consulting scores reached ~80% for Opus 5.5 (metric unlabeled), but ESADE rates tacit C4 judgement 0% replaceable and 74.4% augmentable, and METR saw limited judgement gains: analysis delegates, accountable decisions do not.
evidence.care: Microsoft scores home health aides and nursing assistants 0.04 applicability, and ESADE puts community and social service expert complementarity at 26.8% of time; case notes score under documents, while the in-person relationship stays human.
evidence.physical: ESADE rates manipulation tasks 0.5% replaceable, and Anthropic finds robots cost-competitive for only 0.3% of tasks, roughly 40 years from 10% at a 3% annual cost decline; models contribute only remote guidance.
